heading: Payment gateway developer guide
intro: Everything your developers need to accept wallet payments on your website: create a payment from your server, send the customer to our checkout page, then confirm the result.

overview.title: How it works
overview.description: A payment is a checkout session. Your server creates it with an API key and the customer pays it from their wallet.

steps.createKey: Create an API key on the API keys page and store it on your server.
steps.createSession: When a customer checks out, your server creates a checkout session for the order.
steps.redirect: Redirect the customer to the checkoutUrl from the response. They sign in and pay from their wallet.
steps.return: After paying, the customer is sent back to the returnUrl you gave, with the session id and your order reference added.
steps.confirm: Before you fulfil the order, confirm the payment: either wait for our signed callback or ask the API for the session, and continue only if its status is PAID.

overview.header: Send your key in the {{header}} header on every request

create.title: 1. Create a checkout session
create.description: Call this from your server when the customer is ready to pay. Never call it from the browser, because that would expose your key.
create.returnDescription: About three seconds after a successful payment the checkout page sends the customer to your returnUrl. The page also shows a link back to your site at any time. Treat the return as a hint only: the customer can change the address, so always confirm the status yourself.

request.orderReference: Your own order id. Up to 64 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. It can be used for one session only.
request.amount: Amount in BHD with up to 3 decimals, from 0.100 to 5000.000.
request.description: What the customer is paying for, up to 140 characters. Shown on the checkout page.
request.returnUrl: A full http(s) address on your site, up to 500 characters. The customer is sent there after paying. We add sessionId and orderReference to it.
request.expiresInMinutes: How long the session can be paid, from 1 to 30 minutes. Defaults to 30.

response.id: The session id. Store it with your order.
response.description: The description you sent, or null.
response.status: The current status of the session.
response.payerName: The masked name of the customer once the session is paid, otherwise null.
response.checkoutUrl: The page to send the customer to.
response.expiresAt: The session can be paid until this time, 30 minutes after it was created.
response.paidAt: When it was paid, or null.
response.refundedAt: When it was refunded, or null.
response.returnUrl: The return address you sent, or null.

confirm.title: 2. Confirm the payment
confirm.description: Do not trust the browser redirect on its own. Ask the API for the session, or use the callback below, and check the status before you ship the order.

statuses.PENDING: Waiting for the customer. It can still be paid, cancelled or expire.
statuses.PAID: The money is in your wallet. Fulfil the order.
statuses.CANCELLED: You cancelled it. It can no longer be paid.
statuses.EXPIRED: It was not paid within 30 minutes. Create a new session with a new order reference.
statuses.REFUNDED: You sent the full amount back to the customer.

callback.title: 3. Receive callbacks
callback.description: Set a callback URL on the API keys page and we will tell your server the moment a payment changes, so you do not have to keep asking.
callback.events: We send a JSON POST for each change. The event name is in the body and in the {{header}} header.
callback.signature: {{header}} is the HMAC-SHA256 of the exact request body, in hex, using your signing secret. Reject any call whose signature does not match.
callback.retries: Answer with any 2xx status within 5 seconds. Otherwise we try again, up to 3 times in total. Callbacks can arrive more than once, so make your handler safe to repeat.

manage.title: 4. Cancel or refund
manage.description: Cancel a session that is still pending, or refund a paid one. A refund sends the full amount from your wallet back to the customer and can be done once.

items.get: Get a session and its status.
items.refund: Refund a paid session in full.

errors.title: Errors and rules
errors.description: Every error is a JSON problem document with an HTTP status and a stable code. Branch on the code, not on the text.

items.VALIDATION_FAILED: A field is missing or invalid. The errors object names each field.
items.UNAUTHORIZED: The API key is missing, wrong or revoked. The body is empty.
items.CHECKOUT_NOT_FOUND: No session with this id belongs to you.
items.ORDER_ALREADY_EXISTS: You already created a session for this order reference.
items.CHECKOUT_NOT_PENDING: The session is not pending, so it cannot be cancelled.
items.CHECKOUT_NOT_PAID: Only a paid session can be refunded.
items.INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE: Your wallet balance does not cover the refund.
items.TOO_MANY_REQUESTS: More than 120 gateway requests in a minute with your keys. Wait for the Retry-After header.

items.amount: Amounts are in BHD, from 0.100 to 5000.000, with at most 3 decimals.
items.expiry: A session expires 30 minutes after it is created.
items.order: One session per order reference, so an order can never be paid twice.
items.refund: Refunds are for the full amount and need enough balance in your wallet.
items.rateLimit: The gateway accepts 120 requests per minute per merchant account.
items.secret: Keep the API key on your server. If it leaks, revoke it and create a new one.
items.testing: There is no separate test mode. Try your integration with a small amount, then refund it.
